Gyro-Bohm-normalized linear weight of the perturbed parallel magnetic-field contribution to the parallel component of toroidal gyrocenter momentum flux for a gyrokinetic eigenmode is the normalized eigenmode coefficient for the compressional magnetic contribution to toroidal gyrocenter momentum transport. The perturbed parallel magnetic field is the component of the magnetic perturbation along the equilibrium magnetic-field direction, and the parallel momentum component denotes the part of toroidal gyrocenter momentum carried by gyrocenter motion parallel to that equilibrium field.

The normalization is defined by the ratio of the eigenmode channel contribution to the Gyro-Bohm toroidal-momentum-flux reference:

$$
W_{\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}}^{\delta B_\parallel}
= \frac{\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{GB}}}
$$

where $W_{\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is this quantity, $\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is the perturbed parallel magnetic-field contribution to the flux-surface-normal flux of the parallel component of toroidal gyrocenter momentum for the same eigenmode, and $\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{GB}}$ is the Gyro-Bohm reference for toroidal gyrocenter momentum flux. The subscript $\phi$ denotes toroidal momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is an eigenmode-level linear weight; it is distinct from the spectrum-aggregated [normalized momentum flux due to perturbed parallel magnetic field](name:normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field). It excludes the [perturbed electrostatic-potential channel] and the [perturbed parallel-vector-potential channel](name:normalized_parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).

Sign convention: Positive when the perturbed parallel magnetic-field contribution transports positive toroidal gyrocenter momentum, associated with gyrocenter motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing flux label.

Flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor, or vector of factors, that scales a collisionless free-streaming upper bound on a flux density in a transport closure. It limits the magnitude permitted by that bound while preserving the direction or sign assigned to each resolved flux component by the underlying closure.

For a resolved flux-density component indexed by $i$, a direction-preserving limited flux can be expressed as:

$$
F_i = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_i F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_i$ is the limited flux-density component, $F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure value, $F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming bound, and $L_i$ is the flux limiter coefficient for that component. The limiting range is typically $0 \le L_i \le 1$, with smaller values imposing a stricter cap.

This parent quantity does not specify the transported quantity, resolved component, or spatial region. It covers both generic region-scoped flux limiting, such as the [edge-region flux limiter coefficient], and quantity-specific limiting, such as the [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient); child names identify any additional component or region semantics.

This parent quantity does not specify the transported quantity, resolved component, or spatial region. It covers both generic region-scoped flux limiting, such as the edge-region flux limiter coefficient, and quantity-specific limiting, such as the [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient); child names identify any additional component or region semantics.

Vertical back-surface curvature of an optical element is the signed directional radius of curvature of the back optical surface in its second local tangential aperture direction. The right-handed local optical-surface frame is $(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2, \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b)$ with $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1 \times \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 = \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$, where $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ are the first and second surface-tangential aperture directions and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$ is the positive normal of the back surface; this quantity uses $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$, the object-local aperture vertical direction.

The defining relation is the reciprocal of the signed normal curvature of the back-surface normal section tangent to $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$:

$$
R_{b,2} = \frac{1}{\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)}
$$

where $R_{b,2}$ is the vertical back-surface curvature of the optical element and $\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)$ is the signed normal curvature of the back surface in the $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ direction.

This is a local directional radius, not the scalar parent [optical-element curvature] and not the direction-agnostic [back-surface curvature]. It equals the first-direction radius only for locally spherical or otherwise direction-independent curvature, and it is not a principal, sagittal, or meridional radius unless the surface definition aligns $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ with that direction. Together with an orthogonal directional radius it may characterize simple aligned toroidal curvature, but it does not fully characterize a general aspherical surface.

Absorbed radiated power at a divertor target is the net photon-energy rate deposited on one specified target surface. It includes incident radiative energy absorbed by the target and excludes the reflected portion.

The net absorbed radiative power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the absorbed radiated power, $P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}}$ is the incident radiative power reaching the target, and $P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}$ is the radiative power reflected from the target.

This quantity applies to one divertor target and excludes conductive, convective, charged-particle, and other nonradiative deposition channels. Summation over all divertor targets gives [power of the divertor due to radiation]; the broader radiative deposition concept is described by [power due to radiation].

The vertical neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the vertical component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor for neutral momentum transport along the vertical $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame in multi-fluid edge-plasma models. It bounds the vertical neutral momentum-flux density by the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The vertical component $\alpha_Z$ is defined as the ratio of the magnitude of the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density to its positive free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_Z = \frac{|\Pi_Z|}{\Pi_Z^{\rm free}}, \qquad \Pi_Z^{\rm free} = m_n n_n \left(u_Z^{\rm free}\right)^2
$$

where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density component along $\hat{Z}$, $\Pi_Z^{\rm free}$ is the corresponding free-streaming upper bound, $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number density, and $u_Z^{\rm free}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming reference speed for neutral motion along $\hat{Z}$. The constraint $\alpha_Z \in [0, 1]$ makes the coefficient a magnitude limiter; any sign of the vertical momentum flux is carried by $\Pi_Z$, not by $\alpha_Z$.

This quantity is the vertical member of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) vector and is distinct from the [parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which is taken along the magnetic-field direction, and the [toroidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient], which is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a limiter coefficient, not the neutral momentum-flux density itself.

This quantity is the e-folding distance for a plasma quantity that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The operand may be a particle density, temperature, or heat-flux magnitude.

$$
L_f = \left|\frac{d\ln f}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_f$ is the e-folding length, $f$ is the positive scalar quantity or magnitude being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero.

The general quantity includes the electron number-density specialization [electron decay length](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), the ion number-density specialization [ion decay length], and the heat-flux specialization [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It does not select a species, transport channel, or particular decaying quantity.

The internal inductance $l_i$ is a dimensionless global equilibrium parameter that characterizes the shape of the plasma current density profile. A broadly distributed current results in a lower $l_i$ (near 0.5 for a circular cross-section with uniform current), while a strongly peaked profile raises it toward 2. This quantity enters vertical stability analysis and the plasma–coil circuit equations relating the resistive loop voltage to the time-evolving current distribution.

The $l_{i,3}$ definition relates $l_i$ to the volume integral of the squared poloidal magnetic field:

$$
l_{i,3} = \frac{2}{R_0 \mu_0^2 I_p^2} \int B_p^2 \, dV
$$

where $R_0$ is the reference major radius of the geometric axis, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability, $I_p$ is the total plasma current, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, and the integral is taken over the plasma volume.

The internal inductance is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction using external magnetic measurements, or estimated from the resistive diffusion evolution of the current profile during ramp-up and flat-top phases. In H-mode flat-top conditions, $l_i$ lies in the range 0.7–1.2; sawtooth-free operation and current ramp-up can drive values toward 2. The [total plasma inductance] $L_p$ combines $l_i$ with the external inductance contribution to give the total inductive impedance of the plasma circuit.

This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective, non-diffusive transport of total momentum in the field-parallel direction. It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity associated with total momentum.

For the parallel momentum component, the convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel} P_\parallel
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of parallel momentum, $V_{\mathrm{conv},\parallel}$ is the parallel component of [momentum convection velocity], and $P_\parallel$ is the parallel momentum density.

The parallel component is directed along the local magnetic-field direction. The quantity applies to the total momentum equation without restricting the momentum to ions, neutrals, a species, or a charge state; it therefore differs in population scope from [parallel neutral particle convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) and in direction from [vertical momentum convection velocity](name:vertical_momentum_convection_velocity).

Fast-ion pressure is the kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population, defined through the second central velocity moment of the fast-ion distribution function. It is summed over all ion species and all charge states present in that suprathermal population, so it is the charge-state-summed aggregate of [fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). It excludes the Maxwellian thermal ion contribution represented by [thermal ion pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure).

The tensor is defined as the species and charge-state sum of the second central velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha,q} m_\alpha \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q})\, f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion pressure tensor, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\alpha$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes charge state, $m_\alpha$ is the ion mass for species $\alpha$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}$ is the mean velocity of the corresponding fast-ion subpopulation, $f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal distribution function whose velocity-space integral gives number density, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product.

The tensor may be anisotropic. The scalar fast-ion contribution entering the isotropic [ion pressure] is the trace pressure $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}/3$; for a gyrotropic distribution in the local right-handed field-aligned basis $(\hat{e}_1,\hat{e}_2,\hat{b})$, with $\hat{e}_1 \times \hat{e}_2=\hat{b}$ and $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, this is $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$. Here $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ are the normal stresses parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction; related directional quantities include [parallel total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), [parallel fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure), and [perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure). The scalar fast-ion contribution combines with the thermal contribution in [total ion pressure] when the same population aggregation is used.

The ion momentum convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient in the non-diffusive, advective transport of aggregate ion momentum. It is a transport-closure quantity and is distinct from the material bulk ion velocity, as distinguished from the broader [momentum convection velocity] framework.

A transport-closure decomposition of ion momentum flux is written as

$$
\mathbf{F}_{p,i} = -D_{p,i}\nabla\mathbf{p}_i + \mathbf{V}_{c,i} \otimes \mathbf{p}_i
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum-flux tensor, $D_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum diffusivity, $\mathbf{p}_i$ is ion momentum density, and $\mathbf{V}_{c,i}$ is this convection velocity. The dyadic term represents non-diffusive momentum transport.

The unqualified ion quantity aggregates the ion momentum contribution over all charge states. A species- or charge-state-resolved form, such as [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), supplies the corresponding resolved convention; unlike [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), this coefficient is not the material flow velocity.

The neutral velocity is the mean translational flow of a selected neutral-particle population, whether resolved by internal state or energy range or aggregated over several such populations.

At position $\mathbf r$, it is defined by the first velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{u}_n(\mathbf r)=\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $f_{n,a}$ is phase-space density in m$^{-6}$ s$^3$, $a$ labels included internal-state or energy subpopulations, and $\mathcal A$ is the included set. A resolved form is represented by [neutral internal-state velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity), while aggregation over included states gives a bulk form such as [bulk neutral internal-state velocity]. Vertical, poloidal, parallel, cold, and hot variants select projections or population subsets of this same mean flow.

Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of a multicomponent plasma. It is the velocity whose product with total mass density equals the total plasma momentum density of the species included in the plasma mixture.

The center-of-mass velocity $\mathbf{V}_{cm}$ is defined as total momentum density divided by total mass density:

$$
\mathbf{V}_{cm} = \frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s m_s n_s} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\rho}
$$

where $s$ indexes included plasma species, $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the species fluid velocity entering the [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity) aggregate, $\rho_s=m_s n_s$ is the species contribution to [mass density], and $\rho=\sum_s \rho_s$ is the total [mass density].

The weighting is by mass density, not by charge, number density alone, or an unweighted species average. When [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity) denotes the single-fluid bulk velocity of the same mixture, it is identical to center-of-mass velocity. Projections of this vector define the [radial](name:radial_center_of_mass_velocity), [poloidal](name:poloidal_bulk_center_of_mass_velocity), [toroidal](name:toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity), and [field-parallel](name:parallel_center_of_mass_velocity) center-of-mass velocity components.

documents.before:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum. This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral population; population-qualified standard names identify that population. Each component is a kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport direction, not a full viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$ along direction $\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for momentum-density component $M_j$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{m,i}\,\frac{\partial M_j}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction $\hat{e}_i$ of momentum component $j$, $\chi_{m,i}$ is the directional momentum diffusion coefficient, $M_j$ is the bulk-flow momentum density component of the same transported population, and $x_i$ is distance along $\hat{e}_i$.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel, perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward increasing flux label.

Population-qualified specializations include [plasma momentum diffusion coefficient], [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Scalar specializations include [radial momentum diffusivity] and [ion momentum diffusivity]. This name is the momentum-channel specialization of [diffusion coefficient], and excludes convective momentum transport, external momentum sources, off-diagonal couplings between flux and gradient directions, and the dynamic viscosity-like coefficient obtained by multiplying by mass density.

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive momentum flux is directed opposite to the corresponding gradient of bulk-flow momentum density.

A radial component is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel, perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward increasing flux label.

Population-qualified specializations include plasma momentum diffusion coefficient, [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Scalar specializations include radial momentum diffusivity and ion momentum diffusivity. This name is the momentum-channel specialization of diffusion coefficient, and excludes convective momentum transport, external momentum sources, off-diagonal couplings between flux and gradient directions, and the dynamic viscosity-like coefficient obtained by multiplying by mass density.

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive momentum flux is directed opposite to the corresponding gradient of bulk-flow momentum density.

The ion-state momentum diffusion coefficient encodes the anisotropic diagonal momentum diffusivities for a resolved ion charge state, characterizing how collisional, neoclassical, or turbulent processes scatter that ion population's momentum along the radial, poloidal, and toroidal directions of the device.

In the diffusive closure, the momentum flux density for charge state $s$ along direction $i$ is defined by

$$
\Pi_i^s = -\chi_i^s \, m_s n_s \, \frac{\partial u_i^s}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the number density of that charge state, $u_i^s$ is the flow velocity component along direction $i$, and $\chi_i^s$ is the corresponding momentum diffusivity. Positive values of $\chi_i^s$ indicate down-gradient momentum transport; negative values can arise when turbulent momentum redistribution drives an up-gradient pinch contribution.

The vector form assembles these directional components: the [radial ion-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) governs cross-field transport through flux surfaces, capturing neoclassical viscosity and turbulent Reynolds-stress contributions; the [poloidal ion-state momentum diffusion coefficient] quantifies momentum relaxation along flux surfaces in the poloidal direction. These diffusivities are inferred from global transport analysis, neoclassical theory, or gyrokinetic simulation; typical core values span 0.1–10 m$^2$ s$^{-1}$ in tokamak plasmas. The parent [momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) describes the analogous quantity for bulk plasma without charge-state resolution, and plasma_momentum_diffusivity provides a bulk-plasma effective diffusivity for comparison.

Neutral power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the neutral species per unit volume. It is the aggregate neutral source term in the neutral energy balance, with contributions from the applicable energy-transfer processes.

For a differential volume, the volumetric neutral power density is defined by

$$
p_n = \frac{dE_n}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $E_n$ is the energy transferred to the neutral species, $t$ is time, and $V$ is volume. The quantity is summed over the internal states of the neutral species; [neutral-state power density](name:neutral_state_power_density) resolves the corresponding contribution for one specified state. Positive values denote net energy gain by the neutral species, and negative values denote net energy loss. [Power density] is the unqualified parent quantity covering other recipients and energy channels.

The momentum flux describes the rate at which linear momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It encompasses the convective ram-pressure term, the isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress contributions, and appears as the divergence term in the plasma fluid momentum-balance equation.

The momentum-flux tensor for a single plasma fluid is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho \mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ the bulk flow velocity, $p$ the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$ the viscous stress tensor. The momentum current through a surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is $\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This name is the structural parent for species- and direction-resolved forms. Species-specific instances include [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), and [plasma momentum flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux), each summed over the relevant population. Directional projections such as [parallel momentum flux] isolate field-aligned transport, while [poloidal momentum flux](name:poloidal_momentum_flux) captures cross-field transport through toroidally symmetric surfaces. The complementary volume source density entering the momentum balance is given by [volumetric plasma momentum source].

The ion charge state particle flux vector characterizes the directed flow of ions in a specific ionization stage $z$ through a unit surface per unit time, treating each charge state as a distinct species in charge-state-resolved multi-fluid transport models. This per-stage resolution is essential for modeling impurity accumulation and fuel-ion evolution in confined plasmas, where ionization and recombination continuously couple adjacent charge states.

The flux vector is defined as the first velocity moment of the charge-state population:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z = n_z \mathbf{v}_z
$$

where $n_z$ is the number density of ions in charge state $z$ and $\mathbf{v}_z$ is the mean fluid velocity of that charge-state population.

Directional projections of this vector yield [radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:flux_surface_normal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for cross-field transport across magnetic flux surfaces, [poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for poloidal flow asymmetries, and [parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for field-aligned streaming. The scalar surface-normal analog [ion_state_particle_flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) represents a single-surface projection used in one-dimensional transport approximations.

Charge-state-resolved fluxes are computed in multi-fluid or kinetic transport codes using ionization and recombination rate coefficients from atomic databases. Core plasma values span approximately $10^{18}$–$10^{21}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, while fluxes near plasma-facing components and divertor targets can exceed $10^{22}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$.

Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified fast ion charge state. Orbit classes and directional components select particular contributions without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to the specified fast ion charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the fast-ion, charge-state-resolved realization of [ion charge-state torque density due to collisions]; [co-passing fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [toroidal fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) are orbit-resolved or component-resolved instances.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum, positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

Ion charge-state power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from a specified ion charge state per unit volume. It is the charge-state-resolved ion recipient term in the local ion energy balance, with the recipient belonging to a defined fast or thermal population.

For a differential volume, the volumetric power density is defined by

$$
p_{E,s} = \frac{dE_s}{dt\,dV}
$$

Positive values denote net energy gain by the specified charge state; negative values denote net energy loss. Summing the applicable charge states and ion populations gives [ion power density]. [Fast ion charge-state power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) and [thermal ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) are population-specific instances of this quantity, which specializes [power density].

The diamagnetic drift current density is the conventional electric-current contribution associated with pressure gradients in a magnetized plasma. The parent vector includes the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular term and field-aligned return-current contributions required by current continuity; its projections include the [radial diamagnetic-drift current density] and [vertical diamagnetic-drift current density].

The isotropic-pressure diamagnetic contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia},\perp}=\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field in tesla, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $p$ is the plasma pressure in pascals. This relation gives the perpendicular drive; field-aligned components such as the [parallel diamagnetic-drift current density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [Pfirsch–Schlüter diamagnetic-drift current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) are included when required by the current-density decomposition. The vector quantity retains direction, unlike the [diamagnetic current density] magnitude.

Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the diffusive momentum flux of a specified ion charge state and the negative local gradient of its momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. It describes directional redistribution of momentum for that charge state.

For transport direction $i$, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)} = -D_{m,i}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_i^{(q)}\right)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the diffusive momentum flux, $D_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the corresponding momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of the specified ion charge state, $u_i^{(q)}$ is its flow-velocity component, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the transport direction.

The quantity is general over directional projections, including the cross-flux-surface form represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and the field-aligned form represented by [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). It is resolved for one ion charge state rather than summed over charge states as in [ion momentum diffusivity], and is a charge-state-specific instance of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).
documents.after:

This quantity is the vector contribution to electric current density attributed to momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles. It excludes current contributions assigned to other mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma current density.

The mechanism-resolved current density is defined from the corresponding charged-particle velocity contributions:

$$
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} = \sum_s q_s n_s \mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{in}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of charged species $s$ in C, $n_s$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{in}}$ is the velocity contribution attributed to ion–neutral friction. Neutral particles have zero charge and do not contribute directly to the sum.

The vector may be projected onto cylindrical, poloidal, field-aligned, or other specified directions, including the [radial current-density component](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), [toroidal current-density component](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), and [parallel current-density component](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). Unlike [current density due to collisions], its mechanism attribution is restricted to ion–neutral friction.

Gyro-Bohm-normalized linear contribution of the perturbed parallel vector potential to the parallel-velocity channel of toroidal gyrocenter momentum flux for a gyrokinetic eigenmode is the normalized eigenmode weight for flux-surface-normal transport of toroidal gyrocenter momentum. The parallel-velocity channel is the part whose velocity-space factor is the gyrocenter velocity component parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field; this member retains only the term generated by the perturbed parallel vector potential $\delta A_\parallel$.

The normalized contribution is defined by division by the gyro-Bohm momentum-flux normalization scale:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{v_\parallel\,\mathrm{gc},A_\parallel}^{(m)} = \frac{\Pi_{v_\parallel\,\mathrm{gc},A_\parallel}^{(m)}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}_{v_\parallel\,\mathrm{gc},A_\parallel}^{(m)}$ is this normalized linear eigenmode contribution, $m$ labels the gyrokinetic eigenmode, $\Pi_{v_\parallel\,\mathrm{gc},A_\parallel}^{(m)}$ is the unnormalized flux-surface-normal flux of toroidal gyrocenter momentum carried by the parallel gyrocenter velocity channel and generated by $\delta A_\parallel$, $\delta A_\parallel$ is the component of the perturbed vector potential parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}$ is the positive [gyro-Bohm momentum-flux normalization scale], $\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}=n_{\mathrm{ref}}m_{\mathrm{ref}}c_{s,\mathrm{ref}}^2\rho_*^2$, constructed from the reference density, reference mass, reference sound speed, and the ratio of reference gyroradius to reference macroscopic length.

This quantity isolates the $\delta A_\parallel$ part of the parallel-velocity gyrocenter channel. It excludes the analogous [perturbed-parallel-magnetic-field contribution](name:normalized_parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field), the [perpendicular-velocity channel for the perturbed-parallel-vector-potential term](name:normalized_perpendicular_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), electrostatic-drift contributions, particle momentum flux, and field momentum-stress channels. It is the eigenmode-specific member of the broader [perturbed-parallel-vector-potential momentum-flux channel](name:normalized_parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential); because a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode has arbitrary amplitude, it is a linear weight rather than an absolute fluctuation level.

Sign convention: Positive when the $\delta A_\parallel$ term gives flux-surface-normal transport, toward increasing flux label, of toroidal gyrocenter momentum associated with motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the local ion temperature gradient for the same charge state. It is the charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective, advective, or $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux of charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their [number density], and $T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). The minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an aggregation over charge states. The corresponding charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Directional children include radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for the component associated with $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, and poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient, for the poloidal component.

Ion charge-state energy flux is the signed component of ion charge-state energy-flux density normal to an oriented surface. It gives the rate at which energy carried by ions in one specified ionization charge state crosses the surface per unit area, including convective and conductive contributions when those channels are in scope.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the energy flux $F_{E,k}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,k} = \mathbf{q}_{E,k} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,k}$ is the energy-flux-density vector carried by ions in charge state $k$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive crossing direction.

This quantity is resolved for one ionization charge state and is not summed over charge states. It is the charge-state-specific form of [energy flux], distinct from [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which describes number transport, and from [parallel ion charge-state energy flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux), which restricts the projection to the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion charge-state energy-flux density has a component in the direction of the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface.

Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions of a specified species and charge state leaves a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component for that incident-ion population, not the incident plasma energy flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The ion charge-state recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ for incident species $i$ and charge state $\zeta$ is defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing ion-associated recombination source:

$$
Q^{\mathrm{ion}}_{\mathrm{rec},i,\zeta}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ an ion-associated surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space by an emitted product or quantum, and $d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding sum.

This quantity resolves the incident-ion species and charge state within the ion-associated recombination energy channel. Summing over incident-ion charge states and incident-ion species gives [ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the broader [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) also includes recombination energy channels outside this ion-associated component. It is the energy-weighted counterpart of [particle flux at the wall due to recombination] for the same surface recombination source.

Lower charge-number bound of an ion charge-state bundle is the smallest integer ionization charge number included in that bundle. It defines the minimum endpoint of the charge-state range represented by a grouped ion state.

The lower endpoint is defined by the minimum over the charge-number set represented by the bundle:

$$
Z_{\min} = \min_{Z \in \mathcal{S}} Z
$$

where $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of integer ionization charge numbers included in the ion charge-state bundle and $Z$ denotes an element of that set.

The value is an endpoint of the bundle, not the [ion charge](name:ion_charge) of a selected representative particle, a representative charge, a charge-state average, a net electric charge, or a fractional effective charge. It refines [lower-bound charge] for ion charge-state bundles and is paired with the [ion-state maximum charge number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number) as the upper endpoint; for a bundle containing one charge state, the two endpoint values are equal.

This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for a specified ion species and charge state. It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity of that ion charge state.

For each selected momentum component and transport direction, the convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the momentum convection velocity, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density. The generic [momentum convection velocity] uses the same closure relation across momentum populations.

This charge-state-resolved quantity applies to one ion charge state and excludes summation over other charge states. Its vector may be resolved into radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or field-aligned components; unlike [energy convection velocity], it transports momentum rather than energy. It is distinct from the ion charge state's material flow velocity.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective momentum flux is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum density.

The toroidal momentum convection velocity is the toroidal projection of the effective convection vector $\mathbf{v}^{\rm conv}$ that enters the diffusion-convection decomposition of the radial momentum flux. It quantifies all non-diffusive contributions to toroidal momentum transport — including intrinsic rotation, Coriolis pinch, and turbulence-driven parallel velocity pinch effects — that produce a net radial momentum flux even in the absence of a local momentum-density gradient.

In the standard flux-gradient framework, the radial flux of toroidal momentum $\Gamma_{p_\phi}$ is decomposed as:

$$
\Gamma_{p_\phi} = -D_\phi \frac{\partial (m_i n_i v_\phi)}{\partial r} + v_\phi^{\rm conv} \cdot m_i n_i v_\phi
$$

where $D_\phi$ is the toroidal momentum diffusivity, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the number density, and $v_\phi$ is the toroidal fluid velocity. The convection velocity $v_\phi^{\rm conv}$ is the quantity documented here.

This coefficient is derived from turbulent transport simulations or neoclassical calculations and is central to predicting toroidal rotation profiles in the plasma edge and core regions. It is the toroidal projection of [momentum_convection_velocity](name:momentum_convection_velocity); the corresponding poloidal projection is poloidal_momentum_convection_velocity. Species-resolved neutral variants are [toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) and [toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity). The closely related [toroidal_momentum_velocity](name:toroidal_momentum_convection_velocity) captures the same pinch physics for the radial grid formulation.

Sign convention: Positive when the convection velocity is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above the $+\hat{Z}$ axis).

Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state is the vector of angular rates associated with the bulk flow of that charge-state population. It is charge-state-resolved and excludes density-weighted averaging over other charge states.

For any resolved angular coordinate $q$, the component is the corresponding bulk-flow velocity component divided by the geometric rotation lever arm for that coordinate:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{A}} \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}, \qquad \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}}{h_q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta}$ is the ion-charge-state rotation-frequency vector, $i$ labels the ion species, $\zeta$ labels the charge state, $\mathcal{A}$ is the set of resolved angular coordinate directions, $\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}$ is the bulk velocity vector of the same charge-state population, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}$ is the positive tangent direction of angular coordinate $q$, and $h_q=|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial q|$ is its geometric rotation lever arm. For the toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, $q=\phi$ and $h_\phi=R$, so the component is the [toroidal ion-charge-state rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [ion rotation frequency]. The charge-state-aggregated ion quantity is the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum, because rotation frequency is an intensive bulk-flow quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component corresponds to motion in the positive tangent direction of its associated angular coordinate; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is positive for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is the direct electromagnetic-wave energy transfer rate to the fast, non-thermal ions belonging to one specified charge state, integrated over the full plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{q,\mathrm{wave}} = \int_V p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{q,\mathrm{wave}}$ is the absorbed wave power for charge state $q$, $p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})$ is its local wave-power deposition density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V$ is the full plasma volume.

This is a charge-state-resolved component of [ion charge-state absorbed wave power]: it excludes power transferred subsequently through Coulomb collisions and is not the cumulative value inside a selected flux surface, which is represented by [fast ion charge-state power at inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

Parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of one specified ionization stage along the magnetic-field direction. It represents the field-aligned Fickian part of that stage's thermal-energy transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources, and is the parallel component of [ion charge-state energy diffusivity].

The defining field-aligned closure is

$$
q_{E,z,\parallel} = -\chi_{E,z,\parallel}\nabla_\parallel w_z
$$

where $q_{E,z,\parallel}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the parallel component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ionization stage $z$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field, $\chi_{E,z,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that ionization stage, and $\nabla_\parallel w_z=\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the field-aligned spatial gradient of that density. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport along the magnetic field.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion species or charge states, unlike [ion energy diffusivity](name:ion_energy_diffusivity). It is a coefficient multiplying the thermal-energy-density gradient, not a temperature-gradient heat-transport coefficient unless the relevant density and heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

Parallel ion charge-state velocity is the field-aligned component of the mean bulk fluid velocity for one specified ionization charge state. It is a component of the vector quantity [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), not a charge-state-averaged quantity.

The parallel component is defined by

$$
v_{\parallel,q} = \mathbf{v}_q \cdot \mathbf{b}
$$

where $q$ denotes the specified ionization charge state, $\mathbf{v}_q$ is its mean bulk fluid velocity, and $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

Unlike [parallel ion velocity], this quantity remains resolved for an individual ionization charge state rather than using a density-weighted mean over all charge states.

Sign convention: Positive when the charge-state velocity has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

This quantity is the effective poloidal convection velocity for the energy carried by one specified ion charge state. It is the poloidal component of the [ion charge-state energy convection velocity], representing advective rather than diffusive energy transport.

The poloidal convective energy flux is defined by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}} = v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}\,\mathcal{E}_{i,q}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal convective energy flux, $v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}$ is this effective velocity, $\mathcal{E}_{i,q}$ is the energy density of ion charge state $q$, and $i$ identifies the ion species. The component is expressed in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\theta$ the poloidal coordinate.

This quantity is distinct from the particle-transport velocity [poloidal ion charge-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and from the energy diffusivity [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity).

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective energy flux is directed toward increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$.

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ion charge state $z$, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit tangent generated by increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed radial flux label $\rho$ and fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that charge state, and $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the corresponding poloidal gradient. The radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for one specified ionic charge state, relating its diffusive particle flux in the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction to the corresponding number-density gradient in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The radial diffusive particle flux component is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,q,R}\frac{\partial n_{i,q}}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the $\hat{R}$ component of the diffusive particle flux of ion charge state $q$, $D_{i,q,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient, $n_{i,q}$ is the number density of that charge state, and $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to one resolved ion charge state and excludes charge-state summation, advective particle transport, and nonradial projections. Here radial means the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component; it is not a flux-surface-normal projection and not a derivative with respect to a flux coordinate such as $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) is the direction-unspecified counterpart, the [poloidal ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) is the corresponding poloidal directional form, and [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity) denotes the same Fickian transport coefficient using synonymous terminology. The charge-state-specific scope distinguishes this quantity from the [radial electron diffusion coefficient].

Sign convention: Positive when a negative radial gradient of $n_{i,q}$ produces diffusive particle flux in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial direction. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the radial diffusive particle flux density of that charge state to the negative radial gradient of its number density.

For the radial projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R} = -D_{s,R}\,\nabla_R n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux density of charge state $s$, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_R n_s = \hat{\mathbf{R}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is its derivative along increasing $R$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and applies to one ionization state, unlike the charge-state-averaged [ion diffusivity]. It is the radial counterpart of [ion charge-state diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and is equivalent to [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when the same Fickian closure is used. Radial denotes the cylindrical $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ projection and is not synonymous with a flux-surface-normal projection; convective transport and particle sources or sinks are excluded.

This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque density acting on a specified ion species in a specified charge state. It represents the local source or sink of toroidal angular momentum, without attribution to a particular transport or collisional mechanism.

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}$ is the full torque-density vector for ion species $i$ and charge state $q$. The vector parent is [ion charge state torque density].

The quantity is a total over all contributing processes for the specified ion charge state; process-resolved contributions are distinct quantities.

Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional torque-density vector delivered to trapped thermal ions in a specified ionic charge state. It represents angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb collisions with background charged species.

The toroidal projection is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} \cdot \hat{\phi}

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}}$ is the [trapped thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density], $q$ identifies the ionic charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The volume-averaged mean charge number of an ion charge-state bundle is the volume integral of the local density-weighted mean charge number $\bar{Z}(\mathbf{r})$ normalized by the confined plasma volume $V$:

$$
\langle \bar{Z} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V} \int_V \bar{Z}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $\bar{Z}(\mathbf{r})$ is the [ion charge state average charge number] — the local density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states in the bundle at position $\mathbf{r}$ — and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last-closed flux surface.

This quantity condenses the radial $\bar{Z}$ profile into a single global representative value for transport and power-balance analyzes. It is distinguished from [volume averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge) by its explicit resolution of the charge-state bundle dimension rather than representing only the dominant ionization state.

This quantity is the net rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to selected plasma particles. The selected population may be electrons, ions, or a specified ion charge state, with the result integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the energy of the selected particle population, and the subscript “waves” restricts the energy-transfer rate to direct coupling from the electromagnetic wave field. This is the absorbed component of [wave power](name:wave_power), distinct from electromagnetic power that remains carried by the wave.

The quantity includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes subsequent collisional redistribution between particle populations. Species-resolved and charge-state-resolved instances include [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) and [ion charge-state absorbed wave power].

Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state is the signed toroidal collisional angular-momentum source for that charge state, integrated over the plasma. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total torque is the additive thermal-plus-fast scalar contribution:

$$
\tau^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
=
\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
+
\sum_f \tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies the charge state, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), $\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its axial projection associated with toroidal angular momentum, $f$ indexes fast-ion sub-populations, and $\tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [toroidal fast ion charge-state collisional torque](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) for sub-population $f$.

Only torque due to Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with co-existing charged plasma species is included. This quantity is charge-state resolved, not summed over charge states, and is distinct from the corresponding local [total ion charge-state collisional torque density].

Sign convention: Positive when collisions transfer toroidal angular momentum to the specified ion charge state in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field is the dimensionless, parallel-velocity-weighted electromagnetic contribution to turbulent radial transport of toroidal angular momentum.

The normalized quantity is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel} = \frac{\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{GB}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is the toroidal momentum flux in the parallel velocity-space channel driven by the perturbed parallel magnetic field, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{GB}}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference momentum-flux scale. The perturbation $\delta B_\parallel$ is the magnetic-field-magnitude fluctuation along the equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$.

This is the parallel component of the aggregate [momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field](name:normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field), complementary to the [normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field]. It excludes contributions attributed to the electrostatic potential and the perturbed parallel vector potential, including the [normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential]. The normalization follows the gyrokinetic reference based on outboard-midplane electron density and temperature.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angular momentum flux is directed outward across magnetic flux surfaces, away from the magnetic axis.

Total plasma radiated power is the total rate at which electromagnetic radiation carries energy away from the plasma. It is the full-plasma radiation loss quantity formed from all photon-emission mechanisms, including line radiation, bremsstrahlung, recombination, synchrotron, and any other radiative emission present.

The defining relation is the volume integral of the local radiation power density over the plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is total plasma radiated power, $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the full plasma volume, $p_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the [power density due to radiation](name:power_density_due_to_radiation) at position $\mathbf{r}$, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The scope is the plasma as a whole; the aggregation convention is integration over the full plasma volume together with summation over all electromagnetic emission mechanisms and spectral contributions. It is not a region-restricted quantity such as [radiated power over core region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), and it is not a diagnostic-channel signal or line-of-sight quantity.

[Bremsstrahlung power](name:bremsstrahlung_power) is one radiative contribution when defined for the same plasma population, whereas total plasma radiated power includes all radiative contributions. [Total neutron power] is distinct because it is kinetic energy carried by neutrons rather than electromagnetic radiation. In an energy balance, total plasma radiated power is a non-negative emitted power that enters as a loss according to the balance convention; it is not itself a signed source term.

This quantity is the total energy delivered from the plasma to plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by all incident channels. It represents the area-integrated power arriving at those surfaces before reflection or re-emission.

The total incident power is defined by integrating the incident energy-flux density over the complete plasma-facing area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the total incident power, $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the union of the relevant plasma-facing surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf r)$ is the incident power per unit area at surface position $\mathbf r$, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a differential surface area. The integrand is the area-density counterpart [energy flux at wall]. The total includes all incident energy channels and excludes power emitted from the wall toward the plasma or vacuum.

Normalized toroidal momentum flux from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, restricted to the parallel velocity-space channel, is the gyro-Bohm-normalized flux-surface-normal transport of toroidal angular momentum associated with magnetic-flutter correlations from $\delta A_\parallel$. Toroidal angular momentum is referenced to motion in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The normalized total parallel-channel contribution is defined by the aggregate gyrokinetic flux moment normalized by the gyro-Bohm momentum-flux scale:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\phi,\delta A_\parallel;\parallel}
=
\frac{1}{\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}}
\sum_s \sum_{\mathbf{k}}
\left\langle
\int m_s R v_\parallel b_\phi\,
v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}\,
\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}\,d^3v
\right\rangle
$$

where $s$ labels species, $\mathbf{k}$ labels fluctuation-wavevector contributions, $m_s$ is species mass, $v_\parallel$ is gyrocenter velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $b_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the magnetic-field unit vector, $v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}$ is the flux-surface-normal magnetic-flutter velocity produced by $\delta A_\parallel$ for magnetic-flux label $\chi$, $\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution contribution, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface and turbulence average. The gyro-Bohm scale is $\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}=n_{\mathrm{ref}}T_{\mathrm{ref}}R_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}/a_{\mathrm{ref}})^2$, with $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference density, $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference temperature, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference major radius, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference gyroradius, and $a_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference minor radius.

This quantity has the same parallel velocity-space projection as the [normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential], while the word total denotes aggregation over species and fluctuation contributions within that projection. It excludes the [normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:perpendicular_normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), whose velocity-space projection is perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, and is not the algebraic sum of the parallel and perpendicular projections.

Sign convention: Positive when toroidal angular momentum for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ is transported in the flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing magnetic-flux label in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Normalized toroidal momentum flux from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, restricted to the parallel velocity-space channel, is the gyro-Bohm-normalized flux-surface-normal transport of toroidal angular momentum associated with magnetic-flutter correlations from $\delta A_\parallel$. Toroidal angular momentum is referenced to motion in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The normalized total parallel-channel contribution is defined by the aggregate gyrokinetic flux moment normalized by the gyro-Bohm momentum-flux scale:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\phi,\delta A_\parallel;\parallel}
=
\frac{1}{\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}}
\sum_s \sum_{\mathbf{k}}
\left\langle
\int m_s R v_\parallel b_\phi\,
v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}\,
\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}\,d^3v
\right\rangle
$$

where $s$ labels species, $\mathbf{k}$ labels fluctuation-wavevector contributions, $m_s$ is species mass, $v_\parallel$ is gyrocenter velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $b_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the magnetic-field unit vector, $v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}$ is the flux-surface-normal magnetic-flutter velocity produced by $\delta A_\parallel$ for magnetic-flux label $\chi$, $\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution contribution, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface and turbulence average. The gyro-Bohm scale is $\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}=n_{\mathrm{ref}}T_{\mathrm{ref}}R_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}/a_{\mathrm{ref}})^2$, with $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference density, $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference temperature, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference major radius, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference gyroradius, and $a_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference minor radius.

This quantity has the same parallel velocity-space projection as the normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential, while the word total denotes aggregation over species and fluctuation contributions within that projection. It excludes the [normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:perpendicular_normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), whose velocity-space projection is perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, and is not the algebraic sum of the parallel and perpendicular projections.

Sign convention: Positive when toroidal angular momentum for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ is transported in the flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing magnetic-flux label in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

actions.phrase: normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential

The quantity is the normalized internal inductance of the plasma current distribution. It characterizes the peaking of the poloidal magnetic field generated by the total plasma current, rather than a ratio formed only from a boundary field.

Under the li_3 definition,

$$
l_i = \frac{2}{R_0\mu_0^2 I_p^2} \int_{V_p} B_p^2\,dV
$$

where $l_i$ is the normalized internal inductance, $R_0$ is the reference major radius, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability, $I_p$ is the total signed plasma current, $B_p$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field, $V_p$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is a differential volume element.

This is a global equilibrium quantity. The aggregation is a volume integral of the squared poloidal-field magnitude over the entire plasma volume, normalized by the square of the total plasma current; it does not select a separate species, charge state, orbit class, or localized position.

It is distinct from the dimensional [plasma inductance]: the present quantity includes the reference-radius and vacuum-permeability normalization in the defining expression and is not a local inductance, a flux-surface average, or a boundary-field ratio.

If $L_p$ denotes the [plasma inductance], the normalized quantity is related by $l_i = 2L_p/(R_0\mu_0)$. Thus, under the same reference normalization, a larger value indicates a more strongly concentrated poloidal-field energy distribution associated with the plasma current.

The root-mean-square wave current is the effective magnitude of the oscillatory radio-frequency current carried by one ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap during wave excitation. It is a non-negative scalar that represents the current waveform over an RF cycle.

For an RF period, the RMS current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{RMS}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T_{\mathrm{RF}}}\int_{0}^{T_{\mathrm{RF}}} i^2(t)\,dt}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RMS}}$ is the RMS wave current, $i(t)$ is the instantaneous wave current in the strap, $t$ is time, and $T_{\mathrm{RF}}$ is the RF period. The time origin is arbitrary within the period.

The quantity applies to a single antenna strap and averages over one RF period; it is not a sum over straps or antenna modules. It describes the strap-conductor current associated with the launched wave and excludes plasma current and non-wave direct current.

It is the RMS transformation of the underlying [wave current of antenna strap]. Unlike that parent quantity, it does not retain instantaneous sign or phase. For sinusoidal excitation, it equals the peak current magnitude divided by the square root of two and therefore differs from the [wave current of antenna strap amplitude].

Permeability of a ferritic element is the scalar magnetic constitutive parameter of that individual ferritic body in an isotropic representation. It characterizes how the element's material supports magnetic flux density in response to magnetic field strength at a given magnetic and thermodynamic state.

The scalar constitutive representation is

$$
\mathbf{B} = \mu \mathbf{H}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the [magnetic flux density], $\mathbf{H}$ is the [magnetic field strength], and $\mu$ is the permeability of the ferritic element.

This quantity applies to the ferritic element itself, not to the vacuum region, coils, plasma, or the magnetic system as a whole. It is an absolute permeability, not a dimensionless relative permeability, and its scalar form excludes anisotropic tensor permeability and direction-dependent magnetization response.

Ferritic material is ferromagnetic, so the underlying relation between $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ may be nonlinear, hysteretic, and saturating. A single scalar permeability denotes the effective material coefficient for the stated state of the element; it is not a complete $B$-$H$ curve and does not encode remanent magnetization except insofar as that effect is represented by the state associated with the coefficient.

This quantity is the effective velocity associated with convective transport of the energy density carried by one specified neutral internal state. It is the neutral specialization of the [internal-state energy convection velocity], with directional realizations remaining applicable to radial, poloidal, or field-aligned transport.

For each resolved transport direction, the convective energy-flux component is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state. The quantity applies to the specified state and does not sum over all neutral states. By contrast, [neutral species energy convection velocity] represents the corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective velocity points in the positive orientation assigned to the resolved transport direction, making the convective energy flux positive in that direction.

Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar diffusivity that relates Fickian diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state to the temperature gradient of those same particles. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states, and is independent of any chosen spatial projection.

The isotropic Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s} \nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their number density, $D_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\nabla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the [internal-state energy diffusion coefficient] to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

As the direction-agnostic parent, it is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of momentum density carried by neutrals occupying a specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational internal state. It is the direction-agnostic parent whose directional members identify the direction of flux and gradient, while the transported quantity remains the full momentum vector of that state-resolved neutral population.

For a diagonal directional member in transport direction $j$, the defining Fick law is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial x_j}
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the specified neutral internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j}$ is the vector diffusive flux of momentum through surfaces normal to direction $j$, $D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}$ is the corresponding diagonal momentum diffusion coefficient, $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried by neutrals in state $\alpha$, and $x_j$ is a coordinate increasing along the flux and gradient direction. The superscript $\mathrm{mom}$ labels momentum transport, not a transported momentum component; the minus sign gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$.

This parent covers diagonal directional coefficients only: a directional qualifier selects $j$, the flux and gradient direction, and not a component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$; off-diagonal tensor transport, where a gradient along one direction contributes to flux through another, is outside this standard name. The radial and toroidal directional children use $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the poloidal directional child uses the direction tangent to the poloidal circuit in a meridional plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$.

The defining gradient is the gradient of internal-state momentum density; a form proportional only to a neutral velocity gradient represents the same coefficient only when the state-resolved mass density is uniform or treated outside the gradient. This quantity belongs to the [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) family, has the same internal-state resolution as [internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient], differs from [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) by resolving the neutral population by internal state, and differs from [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) by transporting momentum rather than energy.
